newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firmer, except for gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firmer, except for gas oil.

text.p: Med oil products were firmer, apart from unchanged gas oil, hit by high outright prices.

Gasoline was firmer with futures while the market for Eurograde was fairly balanced. A refiner sold 30,000 tonnes of Med-sourced gasoline to a transatlantic buyer recently, which brought the known total of September-loading European gasoline due to sail west to 300,000 tonnes.

A 7,000 tonne cargo of Eurograde due to load in the middle of October was traded at fob high +$1, fob Fos. Demand for 98 RON gasoline was good into Lavera, where MTBE production has been cut back, and offers were heard at Eurograde barge quotes
+$25 free in pipe Lavera. Other offers were heard out of NWE.
Naphtha was firmer too. A Ras Lanuf and an Alexandria cargo were available for high cif +$4 cif NWE. Bids for pipeline quality were heard at $210 cif NWE.
Gas oil was steady with a weaker tone. Traders said the market was being stifled by high outright prices.

"Demand is there and supply is there. The evidence of this is that every time there is a dip in prices buyers come in, but while high levels persist not very much will get done especially with the prospect of U.S. material coming in," one trader said.
A couple of Russian cargoes were reported to be offered at quotes cif high +$2.0, basis Genoa.
High sulphur cracked fuel was steady to a touch firmer, with fundamentals driving the market rather than rallying crude.
"There's a bullish tone from the crude, but not much," said one trader.
Dealers said prices were talked around Med quotes +$1, but nothing was seen done.
Good bunker spec quality material was still scarce.
The low sulphur cracked sector was supported by a deal done yesterday by a major to an Italian refiner at high cif Med +50 cents cif Italy. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8980
